4-7-25
The claimant reported a side impact at a conrtolled intersection and said the other vehicle entered from the left while
the light was changing. The claim was opened and assigned for review the same day.
4-17-25
Verified the driver against the policy declarations and confirmed the named insured is listed as the operator of the
vehicle involved. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damgae predates the
policy start.
4-27-25
Spoke with the claimant by phone to take a full statement. The account of the approach, the impact point, and the
sequence afterward matched the first report in every detail.
5-16-25
Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and lists the vehicles and
their final rest positions. The responding officer recorded no citations at the time.
5-28-25
Received scene photos from the claimant showing the driver side door and rear quarter panel damage. The images
confirm some of the details described but do not show the signal or the approach path.
7-16-25
Requested statements from nearby businesses and bystanders. No independent witnesses were located, and the
claim will rely on the police report, photos, and the parties' accounts.
8-27-25
Obtained the repair estimate and inspected the vehicle. The pattern and location of the damage are consistent with
the side impact described, and no prior damage to the same panels is recorded in the claim history.
8-31-25
Ran a prior claims and loss history search for the vehicle and the claimant. No earlier damage to this vehicle appears
in any database checked.
9-4-25
The claimant reported neck pain and stiffness the day after the collision and was seen at urgent care. The reported
injury is a neck strain, which fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type.
9-17-25
Medical records show treatment followed a usual course with physical therapy and home exercise. Symptoms
improved steadily, and care tapered off as the claimant recovered. No earlier injury to the same area is known from
the records obtained.
9-27-25
Reviewed the treatment bills and compared them with the injury and the expected recovery timeline. The charges are
consistent with the care documented, and no unusual items were found.
10-26-25

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
